question: Which three fields come together to make up nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Hospital administration, accounting, and public health
options.D: Medicine, engineering, and medical equipment sales

explanation: Nursing informatics is just a smart blend of caring for patients (nursing), working with computers (computer science), and managing data (information science). You'll get the hang of it easily! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main goal of bringing digital tools into hospital wards?

options.A: Increase the administrative workload for ward nurses
options.B: Reduce medical errors and streamline patient care
options.C: Replace all handwritten doctor prescription orders
options.D: Eliminate the need for physical patient assessments

explanation: Digital tools are here to help us, not replace us! They make our daily work smoother and help us catch mistakes before they hurt anyone. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of a Computerized Provider Order Entry (CPOE) system?

options.A: Allowing doctors to enter medical orders directly and reduce handwriting errors
options.B: Helping nurses calculate drug dosages automatically on a calculator
options.C: Tracking the attendance of hospital doctors and nurses
options.D: Allowing patients to view their medical bills from home

explanation: Have you ever tried reading a doctor's rough handwriting? CPOE lets doctors type orders directly, which saves us from guessing and making mistakes! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: A nurse uses a barcode scanner before giving a patient their IV medication. What safety check does this support?

options.A: Measuring the exact flow rate of the intravenous infusion pump
options.B: Ensuring the hospital pharmacy bills the patient correctly for drugs
options.C: Verifying the five rights of medication administration at the bedside
options.D: Recording the nurse's shift hours for human resource tracking

explanation: Scanning the barcode is a quick double-check right at the bedside to make sure we have the right patient, right drug, and right dose! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a big plus of using mobile phones or tablets right at the patient's bedside for charting?

options.A: Real-time documentation immediately at the patient bedside
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital internet subscriptions
options.C: Allowing nurses to make personal phone calls during shifts
options.D: Eliminating the need for physical nursing assessments entirely

explanation: Charting right away means you don't have to trust your tired brain to remember everything at the end of a long shift. Smart, right? [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why does typing notes into a device right away help cut down on clinical mistakes?

options.A: It prevents nurses from forgetting details at the end of the shift
options.B: It automatically diagnoses patient illnesses without lab tests
options.C: It removes the need for verbal shift handover reports
options.D: It stops doctors from changing treatment plans without permission

explanation: Waiting until the end of the shift to write notes leads to guessing and forgotten details. Charting on the go keeps our records sharp and accurate. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) tools?

options.A: Providing free mobile phones to patients with chronic illnesses
options.B: Automatically transmitting patient vital signs from home to hospital dashboards
options.C: Replacing community health workers with automated telephone calls
options.D: Allowing surgeons to perform operations overseas using robotic arms

explanation: RPM lets patients check their vitals at home and send the numbers straight to the hospital. It's like having a nurse checking in from afar! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: How do remote monitoring tools help patients dealing with long-term issues like heart failure?

options.A: Monitoring what food the patient eats throughout the day
options.B: Detecting early signs of clinical deterioration to prevent hospital readmission
options.C: Ensuring the patient never has to visit a physical clinic again
options.D: Curing the underlying disease process without the need for medications

explanation: Catching small changes early means nurses can step in before a tiny symptom turns into a full emergency sending the patient back to the ward. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: Providing evidence-based recommendations to assist clinical decision-making
options.B: Storing digital copies of historical nursing textbooks
options.C: Scheduling nursing shifts and managing ward staff payroll
options.D: Automatically diagnosing patients without requiring physician input

explanation: Think of CDSS as a smart assistant built into the computer that pops up with helpful guidelines and reminders to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of these is a clear example of a Clinical Decision Support System at work?

options.A: A pop-up warning appears on the screen when a nurse enters a drug allergy
options.B: A computer printer automatically prints out the morning vital sign sheet
options.C: A digital camera takes a picture of a healing surgical wound
options.D: A nurse uses a calculator app to convert milligrams to micrograms

explanation: That instant warning message saving you from giving a drug the patient is allergic to? That's CDSS protecting both you and your patient! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h5)

question: What important habit should you practice every time you step away from a hospital computer?

options.A: Leaving the chart open for the next oncoming shift nurse
options.B: Writing the system password on a sticky note nearby
options.C: Turning off the main power switch of the workstation
options.D: Locking the computer screen to protect patient privacy

explanation: Always lock your screen when you walk away! Keeping patient information private is a core part of our professional ethics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)

question: What does 'alert fatigue' mean when nurses deal with too many software pop-ups?

options.A: Desensitization to system warnings caused by a high volume of pop-up notifications
options.B: Physical tiredness experienced by nurses working night shifts on computers
options.C: Battery failure on mobile devices due to excessive alarm usage
options.D: Anxiety caused by learning how to use new electronic health record software

explanation: When computers beep or pop up warnings constantly for minor things, nurses start ignoring them—which is dangerous because a real warning might get missed! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T4#GNS113_U1_T4_h6)
